transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Anita Rao (LumenCare Head of AI), Carlos Mendes (LumenCare Head of IT), Sophie Lee (Privacy Officer)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about 45 minutes, agenda is POC scope focused on data handling — redaction, logging, retention, prompt storage. quick intros?
[00:18] Anita Rao: Hi, Anita here. we run a bunch of clinical summarization workflows, lots of patient notes, so PII is the big one.
[00:27] Carlos Mendes: Carlos, infra lead, focusing on networking and compliance requirements, we may need VPC-/on-prem options.
[00:36] Sophie Lee: Sophie, privacy, I'll focus on retention and legal constraints re: PHI.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Great. Samir is our SE who will cover the technical redaction and bench plan. Samir?
[00:51] Samir Patel: Hi all. quick note: our typical POC covers ingestion, redaction tests, and a performance benchmark across representative payloads. we'll test both hosted and dedicated flows if needed.

[02:05] Samir Patel: To start, can you describe what you consider PII/PHI? e.g. full SSNs, MRNs, free-text with identifiers, images etc.
[02:18] Anita Rao: Mostly text: patient names, MRNs, sometimes scanned notes OCR'd with weird artifacts. we also have some insurance IDs and provider names. no images in this pilot.
[02:30] Sophie Lee: We need to ensure certain fields never leave our environment unredacted. retention should be minimal — ideally prompts not stored persistently, and logs scrubbed of identifiers.

[04:00] Maya Chen: Understood. typical approaches: 1) client-side redaction before sending 2) server-side redaction in the runtime with redact hooks 3) tokenization + PII masking in the prompt layer. each has tradeoffs on fidelity and SLO.
[04:22] Anita Rao: We prefer server-side so we can test Redwood's redaction accuracy, but we need proof that redacted tokens are not persisted.

[05:10] Samir Patel: Right. Redwood can run redaction pipelines in the private flow: you can run an on-prem preprocessor or use our hosted redaction with guaranteed non-persistence of raw prompts if configured. note: transcription sometimes shows up as 'K V cash' instead of KV cache; sorry, habit of dictation.
[05:34] Carlos Mendes: For hosted, we need SOC 2 plus an architecture diagram showing where data at rest sits. for private deploys, we need KMS/HSM integration details.

[06:20] Maya Chen: We'll share SOC2 and KMS notes in the security pack. Regarding prompt storage, by default we store prompts for 30 days for debugging but that can be disabled or reduced. also retention controls can be set per-route.
[06:42] Sophie Lee: 30 days default is too long for PHI. we need an option to set zero retention or ephemeral only for PII-class routes. can Redwood do route-level retention = 0?
[07:00] Samir Patel: Yes, we have per-route retention configs. for PII-sensitive routes you can set retention=0 and enable 'no-logs' mode. caveat: that removes access to historical prompts for debugging unless you turn on encrypted audit logging with limited retention.

[08:15] Anita Rao: We also worry about embeddings storage. we create vectors for search, do those embeddings contain sensitive info? how do you recommend handling?
[08:27] Samir Patel: Best practice: hash or transform PII before embedding, or store embeddings in customer-controlled vector DB (e.g., self-hosted or VPC-hosted). Redwood can avoid persisting embeddings in hosted mode if you use dedicated capacity and point to your vector store.

[09:40] Carlos Mendes: Network-wise we'll likely require VPC peering and no internet egress from the cluster. is that supported for the POC?
[09:51] Maya Chen: Yes, we support VPC peering and private deployments. for a quick POC we can prototype with hosted but enable strict egress rules; for full production you can use Redwood Private.

[11:00] Samir Patel: On logging: We provide structured audit logs that include request IDs, route, model version, and latency. We can redact or omit the prompt text from those logs. we also offer the option to encrypt logs with customer KMS.
[11:22] Sophie Lee: Great — encrypted logs with customer KMS plus prompt redaction in logs is ideal.

[12:35] Maya Chen: Let's cover success criteria for the POC: what does success look like?
[12:45] Anita Rao: Three things: 1) Redaction accuracy: at least 98% detection of known PHI fields on our sample set (we can provide labeled data), 2) Latency: 95th percentile for 512-token prompts under 250ms for inference (we can be flexible), 3) No PII persisted per retention rules and audit logs show no raw prompts.
[13:12] Samir Patel: For latency I'll call out that model choice matters; with quantized LLMs on dedicated GPUs we typically hit 95th perc ~120-200ms for 512 tokens. Hosted CPU fallbacks will be slower. We'll include model variants in the benchmark spreadsheet.
[13:41] Carlos Mendes: Also need throughput targets: for our sampler we'll want up to 150 requests per second during peak. can Redwood dedicate capacity for that?
[13:52] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated capacity can be provisioned. for a POC we usually emulate with burst capacity or run load tests to size the pool. Samir will propose pool sizing.

[15:10] Samir Patel: On benchmarks: we'll run three tests: correctness/redaction test with labeled dataset, latency test with synthetic replay at target QPS, and persistence test verifying retention policies and log contents. we'll run each test multiple times and capture 50/95/99th latency.
[15:35] Anita Rao: For the redaction test we'll supply ~5k labeled samples and a smaller de-identified set. we expect Redwood to show how many left unredacted and where false positives occurred.

[16:20] Samir Patel: Sounds good. we'll instrument the pipeline to report false negatives/positives and include examples. note that OCR errors can make matching harder — we recommend providing OCR-normalized samples.

[17:00] Sophie Lee: Legally we need proof that encrypted backups don't contain raw prompts and a clear deletion process. also, retention for audit logs must be configurable per route.
[17:15] Samir Patel: We can configure route-level retention and provide deletion hooks that call into our retention API. for backups, you'll want to verify snapshot policies; we can sign an appendix confirming backup encryption and retention behavior.

[18:35] Maya Chen: Regarding prompt storage: can we clarify the modes?
[18:40] Samir Patel: Modes: 1) default short-term storage for debugging (configurable), 2) no-persist (prompts not stored), 3) encrypted persistent with customer-managed KMS. also an option to store only hashed prompt fingerprints for dedup/cache use.
[19:00] Carlos Mendes: Hashing fingerprints — does that leak anything? we worry about reversible hashes if the prompt is small.
[19:10] Samir Patel: Fingerprints are designed to be one-way; but if you hash small PII tokens there is risk of dictionary attacks. we recommend salting and/or storing fingerprints only in customer-managed stores.

[20:30] Anita Rao: What about prompt templating? we sometimes include PHI in few-shot examples accidentally. is there a way to scrub those?
[20:40] Samir Patel: We have prompt templating best practices; for the POC we can run a preflight scanner that flags tokens that match your PHI patterns in prompt templates, and optionally replace them with placeholders.

[22:05] Maya Chen: Timeline: proposed 4-week POC: week 0 (set up and data exchange), week 1 run redaction baseline, week 2 run latency/throughput benchmarks, week 3 remediation and repeat tests, week 4 review and pilot decision. does that align?
[22:24] Anita Rao: Yes that's fine. we need a freeze on model changes during benchmarking window.
[22:33] Samir Patel: Agreed. we'll freeze model versions and document them in the benchmark spreadsheet.

[24:10] Carlos Mendes: Any restrictions on stored prompts for debugging if something goes wrong during benchmark? can we enable temporary access only to named engineers?
[24:20] Maya Chen: Yes, access is RBAC-controlled. we can grant time-bound access to specific usernames; everything is logged and can be tied back to the request id.

[25:45] Sophie Lee: For compliance we'll want a short doc explaining how Redwood handles deletion requests and a demo of deletion flow.
[25:55] Samir Patel: We'll include deletion API docs and a short demo video/steps in the security pack.

[27:10] Anita Rao: On metrics: we also want to track quality regressions — e.g., if redaction alters the clinical summary meaning. can you capture signal for content drift or hallucinations?
[27:25] Samir Patel: We can. Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; for the POC we'll set up basic evals that compare outputs on labeled prompts and flag significant changes.

[29:00] Maya Chen: Any procurement or legal blockers we should be aware of?
[29:08] Carlos Mendes: We'll need a standard data processing addendum and security questionnaire answered. procurement timelines might be 2-3 weeks post-POC.

[30:15] Samir Patel: I'll note the security questionnaire and DPA. we'll attach the answers to the pack.

[31:00] Maya Chen: Quick note on cost: POC costs typically cover dedicated burst capacity and engineering time; we'll put an estimated burn and optional committed pricing if you want to continue.
[31:15] Anita Rao: Please include estimated cost scenarios in the spreadsheet — both hosted and dedicated.

[33:10] Samir Patel: For the retention test we'll create synthetic flows that attempt to retrieve deleted prompts and verify API-level deletion returns 404 and logs show deletion events.

[34:05] Sophie Lee: We also need to ensure SSO (SAML) is in place for access control during POC.
[34:15] Maya Chen: Noted. Our SSO integration is standard; we'll include SAML setup steps.

[36:00] Anita Rao: One pragmatic question: will the POC require raw PHI to be sent to Redwood? we prefer to minimize that.
[36:12] Samir Patel: Not required. you can do client-side pseudonymization or send a de-identified subset; for redaction accuracy we prefer a labeled set with identified fields but that can be delivered through secure transfer (SFTP with KMS encryption) or hosted in your VPC.

[37:30] Carlos Mendes: We'll likely provide de-id and a small labeled set via secure transfer. confirm that data in transit is TLS and at rest encrypted.
[37:40] Samir Patel: Yes TLS in transit, at rest AES-256, option for customer-managed KMS.

[39:00] Maya Chen: To recap next steps and owners (quick): Maya send security pack by 4/5, Samir share benchmark plan by 4/6, LumenCare to share sample data by 4/8, schedule bench run week of 4/9.

[40:20] Anita Rao: Sounds good, appreciate the clarity.

[40:35] Sophie Lee: We'll review retention options internally and come back with policy specifics.

[41:10] Maya Chen: Any final questions?

[41:20] Carlos Mendes: None from me.

[41:28] Samir Patel: I'll follow up with the benchmark spreadsheet and the preflight scanner checklist.

[42:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and the pack shortly. talk soon.

End of transcript.

References and links mentioned: Security pack (link to be sent), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared), deletion API docs (in security pack).
